thread:
sophia: Heads-up — after the KMS key rotation last night I noticed console actions that should be Viewer-only (list/read) showing as Editor-level (modify) in the audit stream. Not many yet but definitely suspicious. Anyone else seeing drift?

dan: Hitting the same. Pulled a quick query against the audit index: 3 events with role_change=editor where the UI showed viewer.

kevin: Can you paste the raw event ids? I want to correlate with the role-mapping service logs.

dan: eventIds: evt-8f3, evt-8f4, evt-90a. snippet: ```json
{"id":"evt-8f3","user":"svc-importer","action":"project.update","prev_role":"viewer","new_role":"editor","auth_method":"console-token"}
```

jen: Note — we rolled a new KMS key and the console service restarted while the role-mapper cache was warm. Possible cache deserialization mismatch if KMS decrypt returned different envelope metadata.

sophia: That matches my hypothesis. I saw one stack trace on the console pod: `RoleMapper.deserialize: Missing encryption_version, defaulted to v0` — might have caused fallback to permissive path.

kevin: I'm looking at role-mapper commit history. We added a fallback that treats unknown encryption_version as legacy and merges defaults. If the defaults include editor perms for certain legacy entries that's bad. Opening a quick patch.

alice: For triage: can we freeze role-related deploys and enable read-only mode for the console? We should avoid further writes until we know blast radius. @security-oncall please advise.

security-oncall: Agreed — enable console read-only flag and throttle writes from CLI/SDK for now. I'll coordinate a low-impact window. Also turning on verbose audit ingestion and backing up current index. :shield:

jen: Steps I'm going to run now: 1) rotate role-mapper config to strict-deserialize (no fallback) 2) backfill any missing encryption_version tags by re-decrypting with previous key material 3) re-run policy-validator against the last 24h events. Posting commands:```bash
# toggle read-only
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://console.internal/api/ops/featureflags -d '{"role_writes_enabled":false}'
# increase audit verbosity
curl -XPOST https://telemetry.internal/api/logging -d '{"audits":"debug"}'
```

kevin: Patch ready: change to throw on unknown encryption_version instead of defaulting. Will open PR with rollback steps.

dan: Meanwhile I exported the three suspect events to secure storage and flagged the requestors. Might be a legitimate migration edge but treat as potential privilege escalation.

alice: Can we check KMS key alias mapping? If the new key has different attributes the envelope may look different to older code. `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=<console-role-kms>` or our internal `kms-bot` should show history.

kms-bot: Key console-role-kms: versions: v1(active 2024-11-02 03:12Z), v2(rotated 2026-03-18 01:04Z). v1 metadata: {"envelope":"v1","aad":"roles-v1"}, v2 metadata: {"envelope":"v2","aad":"roles-v2"}.

sophia: So v2 changed AAD tag. Role-mapper v0 only understands roles-v1 -> fallback triggered. That explains mismatch.

kevin: PR link: https://git.internal/r/kevin/role-mapper/428 — I add strict fail + migration task to patch records encrypted with v2 back to v1 envelope prior to mapping.

jen: Agree on migration. Also we need audit backfill to mark any affected sessions and revoke active tokens for impacted principals until validated. I'll run a revoke-list for tokens that issued edits during the window.

dan: Revoke list run result (partial): revoked 4 tokens, notified owners. I'll attach CSV to the incident ticket.

security-oncall: Overall plan approved: 1) freeze role writes (in place) 2) merge strict-deserialize + rollback-ready PR 3) run migration/rehydrate pipeline on a small sample, validate 4) backfill audit marks + revoke tokens 5) re-enable writes after verification. Keep me posted every 30m.

alice: Quick ask for telemetry: record a binary flag on events that went through the fallback code path so we can query easily later. Tag name suggestion: `fallback_deserialize=true`.

sophia: Good idea — adding to the patch. Also adding an alert rule: if fallback_deserialize > 0 for >5 events in 10m, page SRE.

kevin: I'll fast-track the PR for review, add migration job and revert instructions. If anyone wants pair programming on the migration (testing decryption against both keys) ping me.

jen: Running the migration dry-run now on a sample of 50 records. Will post results in 10m.```
